title: Clothes and buying things
cando: describe and compare things, ask for another size and return something

about.text: In this lesson you buy clothes. You compare prices and sizes, and you try things on. Then you read a returns notice. You also take something back to a shop.
goals: Ask: Have you got this in blue? Can I try it on?
Compare things: cheaper, more expensive, better, the best.
Say what is wrong: It's too small. It isn't long enough.
Read a returns notice, and write to a shop.
Take something back and ask for another size or your money back.

chapters.title: Which one do you want?
chapters.text:
In this lesson you buy clothes, and you take something back.
First, Samir buys a jacket for his new job.
The shop assistant asks: Which one do you want?
Samir asks: Have you got it in blue? Can I try it on?
Then he says what is wrong: It's too small.
Listen to how some words join: Can I try it on? Have you got it in blue?

chapters.title: Cheaper, better, too small
chapters.text:
Now the grammar. To compare two things, add er and say than.
The grey jacket is cheaper than the black one.
With long words, say more: more expensive.
For three or more things, say the cheapest, or the most expensive.
Good and bad are different: better, the best. Worse, the worst.
To say something is not right, use too or enough.
Too goes before the word: too small. Enough goes after it: not long enough.

chapters.title: A returns notice
chapters.text:
Next, you read a notice in a clothes shop. It is about returns and exchanges.
When can you take clothes back? What must you bring?
Then you write an email to a shop. Start with Dear, and say what the problem is.

chapters.title: Take it back
chapters.text:
Then you take something back to a shop.
Say what you bought and when. Say the problem: They're too small.
Ask for another size: Can I exchange them for a larger size?
Is there no other size? Then ask: Can I have my money back?

chapters.title: The book
chapters.text:
Last, you read a short story about clothes and shopping.
Read it once for the story. Then read it again and answer the questions.

warmup.prompt: When you buy clothes, what is most important for you?
warmup.note: There is no wrong answer. Many people look at the price first. But always try clothes on, because sizes are different in every shop.

conversation.title: A jacket for work
conversation.setting: Samir starts a new job on Monday. He is in a clothes shop, and he needs a jacket for work.
lines: Yes, please. I need a jacket for work.
We've got these two. Which one do you want?
The black one is sixty pounds. The grey one is forty-five.
So the grey one is cheaper. Have you got it in blue?
Sorry, only in grey. What size are you?
Large, I think. Can I try it on?
Of course. The changing room is over there.
It's too small. The arms aren't long enough.
Try this one. It's the next size.
Yes, this one is better. I'll take it.
Great. Keep your receipt. You can return it in 28 days.

questions.q: Why does Samir need a jacket?
questions.why: Samir says: I need a jacket for work.

questions.q: How much is the grey jacket?
questions.why: The assistant says: The grey one is forty-five.

questions.q: What is the problem when Samir tries on the first jacket?
questions.why: Samir says: It's too small. The arms aren't long enough.

phrases.text: Have you got it in blue?

phrases.use: Asking to put clothes on in the shop.
Saying the size is not right.
Saying what is wrong with it.
You need it to take something back.

words.title: Have you got this in blue?

items.meaning: A short coat. You wear it over a shirt or a T-shirt.
items.example: I need a jacket for work.

items.meaning: Strong blue trousers for every day. The word always ends in s.
items.example: I wear jeans at the weekend.

items.meaning: Clothes for a woman. It goes from the middle of her body down over her legs.
items.example: She wears a long black skirt to work.

items.meaning: A light shirt with short arms. You put it on over your head.
items.example: I need a white T-shirt.

items.meaning: Big, strong shoes. They cover your foot and part of your leg.
items.example: I wear boots when it rains.

items.meaning: You wear them on your feet, inside your shoes.
items.example: A pair of black socks, please.

items.meaning: Two things that go together. Shoes and socks come in pairs.
items.example: I need a new pair of boots.

items.meaning: The colour between black and white.
items.example: The grey jacket is cheaper.

items.meaning: A light red colour.
items.example: She has a pink T-shirt.

items.meaning: The colour of coffee or wood.
items.example: These brown boots are very nice.

items.meaning: The colour of a banana or the sun.
items.example: Have you got this in yellow?

items.meaning: Big. Shops use it for sizes: small, medium, large.
items.example: Have you got this in a large?

items.meaning: Not short. Long jeans cover your feet.
items.example: These jeans are too long.

sound.title: try it on: words that join
sound.explain: When we speak, some words join. Try it on sounds like one word: try-i-ton. Got it in sounds like go-ti-tin. Listen, then say each group.
groups: try it on · put it on · take it off
got it in · got it in blue · got it in a large
lines: Have you got it in blue?
Can I exchange it for a large?

sayIt.instructions: Say Samir's lines. Record yourself, then listen back. Do try it on and got it in sound like one word?
lines: Yes, please. I need a jacket for work.
So the grey one is cheaper. Have you got it in blue?
Large, I think. Can I try it on?
It's too small. The arms aren't long enough.
Yes, this one is better. I'll take it.

spot.instructions: Look at these sentences from the conversation. Two compare jackets. Two say something is not right.
examples: So the grey one is cheaper.
spot.question: Which words compare two jackets? Which words say something is not right? Where do too and enough go?
spot.answer: Cheaper and better compare two things. Too small and not long enough say something is not right. Too goes before small. Enough goes after long.

rules.title: Cheaper, the cheapest; better, the best
rule: Two things: add er, then than: The grey jacket is cheaper than the black one.
Long words: more: The boots are more expensive than the shoes.
Three or more: the cheapest, the most expensive.
good → better → the best. bad → worse → the worst.
Spelling: large → larger, big → bigger, heavy → heavier.

rules.title: Too and enough
rule: too + adjective: It's too small. They're too expensive.
adjective + enough: It isn't long enough. Is it warm enough?
Not big enough means too small.
Ask for another one: Have you got it in a larger size?
rules.mistake: Not: It isn't enough long. Say: It isn't long enough.

practice.q: The grey jacket is £45. The black one is £60. The grey one is ___ .
practice.why: Two things, a short word: cheaper.

practice.q: The boots are ___ than the shoes.
practice.why: A long word takes more: more expensive than.

practice.q: These socks are £3, £5 and £8. The £3 ones are the ___ .
practice.why: Three or more things: the cheapest.

practice.q: This T-shirt is good, but that one is ___ .
Everything here is cheap and good. It's the ___ shop in town.
practice.why: Number one of all the shops: the best.

practice.q: These jeans are ___ long. I can't walk in them.
practice.why: Too long: longer than you want.

practice.q: The jacket isn't warm ___ for the winter.
practice.why: Enough goes after the adjective: warm enough.
Enough goes after the adjective: big enough.

practice.q: The skirt is £20. The dress is £35. The skirt is cheaper ___ the dress.
practice.why: Compare two things with than: cheaper than.

practice.q: This size is too small. Have you got a ___ one?

yourTurn.prompt: You want to buy a pair of boots. Look at two pairs in a shop, and compare them. Then say one thing that is not right, with too or enough.
starters: The brown boots are cheaper than …
The black boots are better because …
yourTurn.model: The brown boots are cheaper than the black boots. But the black boots are warmer, and they're more comfortable. The brown boots are too small, and they aren't warm enough. I think the black ones are the best for me.

text.title: Returns and exchanges
text.body:
PRACTICE: this shop is not real.

NORTHGATE CLOTHING
RETURNS AND EXCHANGES

Is something wrong? No problem!
You can return or exchange clothes in 28 days.
Please bring:
· your receipt
· the clothes, with the labels on them
Please do not wash or wear the clothes first.

WITH A RECEIPT
You can have your money back. Or you can exchange the clothes for a different size or colour.

NO RECEIPT?
You can exchange the clothes. We can't give you your money back.

SALE CLOTHES
You can exchange sale clothes in 14 days. You can't have your money back.

We can't take back socks.
Questions? Please ask at the till.

gist.a: taking clothes back to the shop

gist.q: Can you take clothes back to this shop?
gist.why: The notice says: You can return or exchange clothes in 28 days.

detail.q: You haven't got the receipt. What can you do?
detail.why: No receipt? You can exchange the clothes, but you can't have your money back.

detail.q: You bought a skirt in the sale. What can you do?
detail.why: Sale clothes: you can exchange them in 14 days. No money back.

detail.a: the receipt and the clothes, with the labels on them
detail.why: Please bring your receipt and the clothes, with the labels on them.

detail.q: Which of these can't you take back?
detail.why: The notice says: We can't take back socks.

items.meaning: To take something back to the shop.
items.example: Can I return these boots?

items.meaning: To give something back to the shop and get a different one.
items.example: Can I exchange this for a larger size?

items.meaning: To have something for a long time and not lose it.
items.example: Keep your receipt.

items.meaning: Not right, not correct.
items.example: It's the wrong size.

items.meaning: Something that is wrong. You need to change it or do something.
items.example: There's a problem with my jacket.

items.meaning: Not different: one is just like the other.
items.example: Can I have the same jacket in a larger size?

items.meaning: Not the same.
items.example: Can I have a different colour?

items.meaning: You write it before a name at the start of a letter or an email. In British English, it can also mean expensive.
items.example: Dear Sir or Madam, I bought a jacket in your shop last week.

model.title: An email to a shop
model.body:
Dear Sir or Madam,
I bought a pair of jeans in your shop on Saturday.
They are too long, and they aren't big enough.
I haven't got the receipt, but I paid by card.
Can I exchange them for a different size?
I can come to the shop on Friday afternoon.
Best wishes,
Mei Chen

write.task: Write an email to a shop. You want to take something back. Say what you bought and when. Say what the problem is. Then say what you want: a different size, a different colour or your money back.
checklist: I started with Dear, and I ended with my name.
I said what I bought and when.
I said the problem with too or enough.
I asked a question: Can I exchange …? Can I have my money back?

card.title: Take it back
card.situation: Last week you bought a pair of boots for work. At home, you tried them on again. They are too small. You have the receipt.
card.goal: Go back to the shop. Say what the problem is, and ask for a larger size. If there isn't one, ask for your money back.

phrases: I bought these boots here last week.
Can I exchange them for a larger size?
Can I have my money back, then?
prepare.notes: Write what you bought, when, what the problem is, and what you want. Have your receipt ready.

doIt.liveClass: In the live class, your teacher is the shop assistant. Buy something, then take it back and explain the problem. Then change roles.
doIt.wehel: You are a shop assistant in a clothes shop. First, I buy something from you. Then I come back, and I want to return it. Ask me what the problem is, and ask for my receipt. Offer me a different size or my money back. Use simple English.

model.title: At the shop again
lines: Yes, please. I bought these boots here last week, but there's a problem.
Oh, I'm sorry. What's wrong with them?
They're too small. My feet hurt.
They're a size 8. Can I exchange them for a 9?
Sorry, we haven't got a 9 in brown. We've only got a 9 in black.
I don't like the black ones. Can I have my money back, then?
Yes, of course. The money goes back on your card.
That's fine. Thanks for your help.
compare: Did you say what you bought and when?
Did you say the problem with too or enough?
Did you ask for a different size?
Did you ask for your money back when there was no size?

canDo: I can describe clothes: the colour, the size and the price.
I can compare things: cheaper, better, the best.
I can say what is wrong: It's too small. It isn't long enough.
I can read a returns notice and write to a shop.
I can take something back and ask for another size or my money back.

reading.before: Look at the title and the first picture. What is the person buying? Is there a problem?
reading.talk: Did the person in the story buy the right thing? Do you like shopping for clothes in town, or do you buy online? Write two or three sentences, or say them to Wehel.

quiz.q: The grey jacket is ___ than the black one.
Everything is good here. It's the ___ shop in town.
quiz.why: Number one of all: the best.

quiz.q: The jacket is too ___ . I need a larger size.
quiz.why: You need a larger size, so it's too small.
Enough goes after the adjective: warm enough.
Try it on: put it on to see if it is right.

quiz.q: Can I ___ these boots for a larger size?
quiz.why: Exchange: give it back and get a different one.

quiz.q: ___ your receipt. You need it to take something back.
quiz.why: Keep the receipt: don't lose it.

quiz.q: My feet ___ . These shoes are too small.
quiz.why: Two feet, so hurt, with no s.

quiz.q: A ___ of cheese, please. About 250 grams.
quiz.why: You cut a piece from a big cheese.

liveClass: Day 1: practise the shop conversation in pairs. Then change the clothes, the colours and the sizes: Have you got this in …?
Day 2: compare three things the class can see: bags, phones, coats. Which is the cheapest? Which is the best? Then say what is wrong with too and enough.
Day 3: the returns desk. You are the shop assistant. Each learner takes something back, says the problem, and asks for another size or their money back.
Day 4: talk about the book, answer questions, and let two learners read their emails to the shop aloud.
